aions_core/agi_core.py: This file implements a reasoning engine that processes queries through multiple thinking layers including understanding, planning, execution, reflection, and learning. It tracks goals, working memory, and reasoning chains to build confidence scores in its answers. The system can perform multi-hop reasoning over knowledge concepts and extract strategic patterns from successful interactions. It integrates with the CBMS memory system to retrieve and synthesize knowledge from stored chunks, maintaining performance metrics and learning from past queries to improve future reasoning.
aions_core/agi_unified.py: This file brings together multiple AI system components into one interface that can operate in symbolic, neural, or hybrid mode. It manages parallel processing through worker threads for learning and evolution cycles triggered during interactions. The system gracefully handles cases where specific components fail, falling back to alternatives while tracking performance across all active modules. It implements task execution through an agent layer and can apply style preferences to responses before returning them to users.
aions_core/aions_reformed_integration.py: This file loads seed data from JSONL files to answer factual questions about capitals, mathematics, programming, science, history, and Polish language without calling external services. It checks patches first for critical fixes, then aliases, then searches through specialized knowledge bases organized by domain with fallback to a unified memory system. The query path prioritizes exact matches, applies scoring to find the best answer, and returns confidence levels along with the source of information. It filters out polluted or irrelevant responses that don't match what was actually asked.
aions_core/cbms_memory.py: This file manages a chunked knowledge storage system that saves and retrieves pieces of information identified by unique identifiers, organizing them by concepts for quick lookup. It implements Korean-style key indexing for fast retrieval and optional symbolic encoding for enhanced search capabilities. The system logs thinking sessions as records when queries are processed, tracks access patterns on stored chunks, and creates new chunks when significant insights emerge from analysis. It can serialize and deserialize knowledge to disk while maintaining an index of what exists.
aions_core/server/cbms_doctor.py: This file scans a directory of JSON chunk files and reports consistency problems including unreadable files, missing core fields, content that is empty or suspiciously small, size declarations that don't match actual content length, and references pointing to non-existent chunks. It categorizes findings by severity and provides statistics about chunk health, orphaned items with no incoming references, and schema drift where individual chunks have unusual fields. The tool operates read-only and outputs results in human-readable or JSON format to help detect data decay in long-running systems.
aions_core/server/codebook_engine.py: This file manages a bidirectional mapping between Esperanto text phrases and CBMS symbolic codes stored in a codebook JSON file. It uses greedy phrase matching with longest-first precedence to encode natural language into symbol sequences, allowing multiple phrases to map to the same code. The decoder reverses the process by looking up codes and reconstructing natural language text. This enables more compact semantic representation of queries and responses in a symbolic space.
aions_core/server/generator_cbms.py: This file composes structured answers from knowledge chunks by loading their content, formatting them with context about the query, conversation history, and CRLA tournament results. It synthesizes key points from multiple chunks while respecting a maximum number to include, and preserves bracketed source citations and numerical sequences to avoid losing structured information. The output is formatted in Polish with headers, bullet points for key information, and metadata about how many chunks were used.
aions_core/server/stylist.py: This file applies lightweight stylistic cleanup to text answers including whitespace normalization, ensuring source citations are on new paragraphs, and capitalizing the first letter if needed. It validates that no facts or numbers are changed during styling by checking bracketed blocks and numeric sequences remain intact, refusing to apply changes if invariants are violated. The tool reports whether changes were applied and why if it declined to style something.
aions_core/tools/bench_runner.py: This file repeatedly sends a fixed set of test queries to a local chat API endpoint and records response times and whether they indicate refusal or success. It collects raw latency data in JSONL format and computes summary statistics including median and 95th percentile response times per query. The results are saved to both a line-delimited log file for detailed inspection and a JSON summary for monitoring performance trends over time.
aions_core/tools/query_db.py: This file opens a SQLite database storing file scanning results and queries which folder contains the most JSON chunk files, displaying the counts and paths for the top ten matches. It is used to understand where knowledge chunks are concentrated in the scanned filesystem.
aions_core/unified_core.py: This file integrates multiple AIONS subsystems including core reasoning, vector enhancement, hybrid retrieval, agent planning, style controllers, and monitoring into one v2.0 interface while maintaining backward compatibility with v1.0. It attempts to load each component gracefully, reporting which ones succeeded or failed, and routes queries through the best available processing path with fallback chains when primary methods fail. The system tracks statistics on query counts, fallbacks, and applies style profiles before returning answers.
control_plane/agents/agent_schema.py: This file defines the structure of agent role definitions stored in agent.json files using strict validation where all required fields must be present and non-empty. Each agent has an identifier, type, name, description, list of allowed skills with wildcard patterns, risk ceiling, model tier, system prompt template, and version. The validation fails the entire agent definition if any required field is missing or wrong, preventing invalid agents from being registered.
control_plane/cbms_gate.py: This file implements a retrieval-gated response system that answers questions from local knowledge chunks if confidence is high enough, only calling a language model when confidence is below a threshold. It uses multiple retrieval strategies including Korean-style keys, lexical scoring, codebook symbol matching, and optional Chroma vector search, caching results to avoid recomputation within and across processes. The gate composes answers directly from chunks without an LLM when hitting, and enriches prompts with retrieved context when missing to help the LLM provide grounded answers.
control_plane/node_agent/agent.py: This file runs as a lightweight daemon on a Linux worker machine that registers itself with central AIONS core, sends periodic health heartbeats, and exposes an HTTP API for remote shell command execution. It collects host metrics including CPU load, memory usage, and disk space from the proc filesystem and reports them to the core server. All commands have a 60-second timeout and responses are capped at 64KB to prevent memory exhaustion from large outputs.
control_plane/orchestrator_loop.py: This file runs a minimal local understand-act-remember loop that processes user queries through intent detection, knowledge retrieval via CBMS gate, and response generation from context alone without using external services. It optionally stores interaction records in a Chroma memory system for recall during future sessions. The system produces JSON output documenting the processing path taken and success/failure status.
control_plane/skills/executor.py: This file runs individual skills or chains of skills in sequence, checking world state conditions to skip skills when appropriate and enforcing security gate approvals before execution. It resolves variable references from previous step outputs, records execution success and timing for each skill, and audits all attempts. Chains stop on first failure unless verification passes, enabling learn-before-save workflows that only save successful sequences.
control_plane/skills/papiery.py: This file stores personal administrative items like tasks and notes as individual JSON files in a shared folder, treating each item like a CBMS block with title, deadline, priority, status, and tags. It provides functions to add new items, list open tasks sorted by deadline and priority, find due items within a time window, mark items done, and search by keyword.
control_plane/skills/stats.py: This file maintains multidimensional statistics on skill execution including success count, failure count, average execution time, and success rate, computing a confidence score that balances reliability and speed. Statistics are persisted to disk and can be ranked using different preference weights for fast, reliable, or balanced scoring. This enables the system to choose between multiple skills that accomplish the same goal.
mcpServers/VS_CODE_MCP_CODEX/src/desktop: This file provides an abstraction layer for desktop automation operations across Windows and Linux platforms, with platform-specific implementations for screenshot capture, mouse clicks, keyboard input, window management, and shell command execution. On Windows it delegates to a binary control module, while on Linux it uses xdotool for input and mss for screenshots. The base class defines the interface that all providers must implement, with disabled and unavailable variants for fallback cases.
mcpServers/VS_CODE_MCP_CODEX/src/test_se: This file implements a minimal test MCP server with ping, echo, and health check tools to verify that the MCP framework is working correctly. It uses FastMCP for simplified server setup and logs startup and tool invocation events for debugging.
scripts/calendar_e2e_smoke.py: This file verifies Google Calendar integration by testing that an OAuth token exists, connecting to the Google Calendar API, and retrieving today's events, tomorrow's events, and the next ten upcoming events. It checks that token refresh mechanisms work and never prints sensitive information like tokens or client secrets. The script serves as a smoke test to confirm the end-to-end calendar pipeline is operational.
scripts/demo_secretary.py: This file demonstrates the skill engine operating as a personal secretary by showing current time, user identity, open windows, recent workspace files, and system resources. It sends notifications to the desktop, learns a new recipe for note-taking with dates, and demonstrates skill discovery and ranking. The script showcases the full workflow from task decomposition to learning from successful execution.
scripts/full_system_scan.py: This file orchestrates multi-drive system scanning using the Everything file indexing tool and a turbo code graph scanner, detecting project roots by looking for markers like .git or package.json, and building a consolidated master map of all discovered projects and their relationships. It stages scans by drive and generates per-drive summaries, handling timeouts and errors gracefully. The results include inventory counts, code files analyzed, and project metadata.
scripts/project_scanner.py: This file comprehensively scans source code directories to build a dependency graph, detect duplicate files by content hash, identify orphaned code that nothing imports, find heavily-imported hub files, and detect circular dependencies. It categorizes files by type and location, parses imports from Python, JavaScript, JSON, Markdown, shell, and PowerShell files, and generates markdown reports with statistics and analysis of code health.
scripts/sync_dev_mirror.sh: This file uses rsync to one-way sync files from the E: drive to a WSL development mirror on D: drive, excluding virtual environments, Chroma data, scan results, and Python caches to save space. It supports dry-run mode to preview changes, mirror mode to delete files not in source, and an option to include .git directories. Configuration can be overridden via environment variables.
scripts/test_skill_engine_foundation.py: This file tests the core skill engine functionality including skill discovery, type-agnostic retrieval by semantic matching, chaining multiple skills into a multi-step task, verifying success before learning, saving and replaying recipes, and tracking multidimensional statistics on skill performance. It confirms that recipes are cached and reused when the same intent is encountered again.
scripts/vault/seal_secret.py: This file encrypts plaintext secret files into a local DPAPI vault using Windows Data Protection, storing them with a human-readable label in an index file. The script ensures secrets are sealed before ever being checked into version control and provides the path where the sealed file is stored for future retrieval.
server/models.py: This file defines Pydantic data models for the context retrieval and session management API including structures for adding documents to sessions, searching across them, getting session information, dumping entire session contents, pruning old entries, and viewing system health statistics. Models support metadata filtering, keyword bias boosting, and tracking which agents have used each session.
